questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to take classes with more of a cognitive neuropsychological focus. This was possible at department of Psychology, but also Berlin School of Mind & Brain.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I am very happy that I went and loved most of my classes, but I was very left alone through the entire thing. I wish I would have known that I would be the only Erasmus student in all of my classes!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay looking in Agnes for courses, but tough to figure out what my chances were for getting into the classes.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I e-mailed back and forth with the Erasmus coordinator. I was initially a bit chocked that it was only possible for me to take courses equivalent to 9 (!) ECTS points due to a lack of classes in English. I had been falsely informed that everything would be in English, but apparently there was still an adjustment period at that time. When I got very frustrated, I still could not get any meetings or phone calls with anyone, only communication on e-mail. This was highly frustrating and tedious!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Only Zoom meetings, even in spring 2022. I really wish there had been some introduction in person.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It is hard to find accommodation in Berlin, especially for internationals. Because I had classes at Charité (Mitte) and in Adlershof (a bit far outside the city), it was important for me to live near public transport. I ended up booking a room through
Uniplaces.com
which was great in terms of location, but horrible regarding cleaning (was honestly gross when I moved in). Definitely overpriced, but nice to have guaranteed housing before going there.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I don't know, I have never lived on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: German bureaucracy definitely lives up to its reputation. Other than the joy in feeling like the main character in a Kafka novel, this was very stressful and complicated.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Could be easy if you could simply sign up on their platform (Agnes) - however, to get specific class approved, they must be grouped together in modules of 3-4-ish which made everything very complicated. I had to get special permission to join a lecture series at School of Mind & Brain to be able to take classes at department of Psychology which was easy when e-mailing a specific professor who knew some people there - but I had no chance of getting enough credits on my own.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Erasmus coordinator on e-mail (took lots of work), direct help from professors.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up getting every class I wanted, but there was only enough in English for me to take 22,5 ECTS. Also, none of these classes were the same as the ones I got pre-approval for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I hope it will be easier from this year where everything should really be in English. If you end up in problems, try contacting your teacher directly and explain your situation - they might have more power than they typically do in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very happy to be able to focus completely on cognitive- and neuropsychology, also in methods and electives.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Much higher level in statistics. I took a class where the description said no specific knowledge was required, but the level among German psychology students is much higher in statistics. High level (maybe too high for most students) at the seminars at School of Mind & Brain. On the other hand, I went a few times to a clinical psychology seminar where I would say the level is much lower than at UCPH. They go about it completely differently and discuss the themes of paper intuitively without any additional theoretical perspectives.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More traditional dynamics between teachers and students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Fundaments of the Mind and Higher Cognition
Advanced Longitudinal Data Analysis
Principles and challenges of 'brain reading'
Memory and the Brain
Scientific explanations in cognitive neuroscience
Neuroimaging

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The longitudinal data analysis class was very interesting and new to me, but also super challenging. 
Scientific explanations in cognitive neuroscience was the first time I have encountered in-depth philosophy of science discussions within the natural sciences, also very cool. I also loved Memory and the Brain with very good literature and inspiring Professor (Roberto Cabeza).

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not know you were required to buy a student local transportation card. This plus some extra (smaller) fee cost me around 2000 DKK.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was less expensive and I did not have to buy any books.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I know there were sports, I did not use that.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: See above.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I don't know. There was not much.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Berlin is amazing! You definitely have to try clubbing there, otherwise the many museums, flee markets, shopping.. Also nice to go see other cities, I went to Dresden and Leipzig for weekend trips.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Harder than expected, since we are neighboring countries. Also, I was sometimes the only non-German speaker in a class, making it a bit awkward to stand my ground on the class being held in English as promised. Luckily oftentimes the students would help me with this.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No -  I almost didn't other than minimal small talk. I wish there had been done something from their side to make it a bit easier, but I ended up just meeting people in other ways (e.g., Bumble for friends, Erasmus meet ups, dating apps...)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Bureaucracy, less transparency in who has power over what. Using more formal language (calling teachers by last name, for example).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Berlin culture is very tolerant which I find very cool. Also a lot of internationals, making it easy to make friends outside of uni.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
All for psychology, specifically:
1. Only go there if you are into neuro- or cognitive psychology. My impression of other disciplines is pretty bad.
2. Make sure to live close to the S-Bahn. The psychology department is in Adlershof, which is a bit far away from most popular areas. I also made sure to live on the east side of the city for the same reason. 
3. Be prepared to do everything on your own with not much help. This goes for academic as well as social stuff.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If I could change something, I would have signed up for the HU German classes. I didn't because it was on Zoom and a bit expensive, but I saw that other people made many friends that way.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Super cool neuropsychology classes, very challenging but made it through. Also met my boyfriend hehe.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting enough classes. And the summer semester runs from late April with the last exams in late September, so now I am working on a big exam while also having started a new semester at home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Nejjj

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
